transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, doctor, I... I wasn't really sure about coming in today, but I just don't know what else to do at this point. I work as a personal care aide, you see, and it's hard work, long hours on my feet taking care of people, so when I get home to my little studio apartment, I just want some peace and quiet. But I came in because... well, I keep hearing these voices. And I don't mean like a faint mumble through the walls from the neighbors or the building's pipes acting up. I mean it's as clear as somebody standing right there in the middle of my room with me. 

They keep saying my name, over and over, and telling me my work is being judged. They talk about my job and how I'm doing things and just judging every little thing I do. And the absolute scariest part is, the house is completely quiet. I know for a fact nobody is there. I live alone, the deadbolt is locked, the TV isn't even on sometimes, but the voice is right there, just as real as you talking to me right now. I'll just be sitting on the edge of my bed trying to rest my feet after a shift, and suddenly they start up, calling my name and evaluating me, and I look around and the room is totally empty. I just can't make them stop no matter what I do, and it's driving me out of my mind because I know I'm the only one in that apartment...
About how long ago did you first start hearing these voices?

Oh, goodness, let me think back... it feels like a lifetime, honestly, but if I really look at the calendar, it’s been about nine months now. Nine whole months. I remember because it was right around the time the weather started changing last year, and I was picking up extra weekend shifts to help cover my rent. At first, I thought maybe I was just overtired, you know? Lifting grown adults out of wheelchairs and changing beds all day, it really takes a toll on a person my age. You get home and your ears are just ringing from exhaustion. 

But it didn't go away with a good night's sleep. For nine months, I've had to listen to them. And it’s not just the voices in my apartment, doctor, it’s this... this constant, heavy fear I have that my work is actually being watched. I go to my clients' houses, and I'm just looking over my shoulder the entire time, terrified someone is secretly monitoring how I fold the linens or how I measure out their morning pills. I just absolutely know I'm being watched and evaluated by someone, and then I go home to my empty apartment and those voices start up and confirm it, telling me everything I did wrong. 

Day in and day out since last year. I haven't had a single moment's peace. You try giving an elderly man a sponge bath when you can feel eyes staring right at the back of your neck, taking notes on every little move you make. It's impossible. It just wears you down to the absolute bone, living like this for nine months, always looking over your shoulder, always waiting for the voices to start judging you the second you sit down...
Over these past nine months, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness or depression?

Sadness? Depression? Well, doctor, I... no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I've been depressed or anything like that. I just... I don't have time to be sad, honestly. Between the long hours at work and coming home to those voices constantly judging me, I'm just too on edge all the time. I mean, sure, I'm exhausted, and it's terrible living with this fear that I'm being watched every second of the day, but it's not like I'm sitting around crying or feeling hopeless in that way. It's more of a... a constant anxiety, a feeling of being hunted, almost. 

Like I said, I'll be at a client's house, and I'm just so focused on doing everything perfectly because I know someone is watching me, taking notes on how I prepare their meals or how I help them out of the shower. And then I get home, and the voices start up, and I'm just trying to figure out how to make them stop, how to get just five minutes of quiet so I can rest my eyes. There's just no room for sadness when you're constantly trying to defend yourself against something you can't even see. I mean, maybe someone else would be depressed in my shoes, but for me, it's just this overwhelming stress and fear. I just want it to stop so I can go back to being a normal person who just goes to work and comes home to a quiet apartment, you know? That's all I really want, just a little bit of peace...
Do you have any physical health conditions or medical illnesses that you're being treated for?

Physical health conditions? Oh, no, doctor, no. I mean, thank the Lord for small mercies, right? Because if I had to deal with high blood pressure or diabetes or something on top of all this... I just don't know how I'd manage it. I really don't. My body is tired, don't get me wrong. When you're fifty-five and you spend your whole day lifting people, turning them in bed, pushing heavy wheelchairs over thick carpets... well, your back aches and your feet swell up like balloons by the end of the day. But that's just the job, you know? That's not a medical condition, that's just being a personal care aide for years and years without a proper break. 

I don't take any pills for anything, except maybe an aspirin when my knees are really acting up after a long shift. I haven't even seen a regular doctor in... gosh, I don't even know how long. I just never had the need, or the time, really. I mean, between the bus ride to work, the long shifts, and then coming home to... well, to the voices and the feeling of being watched... who has time to sit in a waiting room for a physical? I've always been sturdy, always been a hard worker. Never had heart problems, no asthma, no thyroid issues, nothing like that. It's just my mind, doctor. It's just this constant, terrible feeling that I'm being judged, and those voices... physically, I'm fine, but mentally, I'm just so worn out. I just wish my mind could be as healthy as my body, you know? Because physically, I'm strong as an ox, but this other stuff... it's just breaking me down.
Do you drink alcohol or use any recreational substances or street drugs?

Oh, heavens no, doctor. Alcohol? Drugs? Never in my life. I mean, I see people on the bus when I'm commuting to my clients' houses, and you can just smell the liquor on them at six in the morning, or they're nodding off from whatever they bought on the street. It just breaks my heart, but it also makes me think, how on earth do they function? I have a hard enough time just trying to get through my day with these voices constantly picking at me and that horrible feeling of being watched. If I added a drink to that... well, I just can't even imagine. It would probably just make the voices louder, wouldn't it? 

Plus, my job requires me to be sharp, you know? I'm handling other people's medications, doctor. I'm popping out blood thinners and heart pills for eighty-year-old men and women who rely on me to get it exactly right. If I had a glass of wine or a beer, my hands might shake, or I might misread a label, and then where would I be? And then the voices would really have something to yell at me about, wouldn't they? They'd be screaming that I did it wrong, that the person watching me caught me making a mistake. I just couldn't risk it. 

So no, not a drop of alcohol, and certainly no street drugs. I don't even buy cooking sherry for the kitchen. I just drink my tap water and my instant coffee. And honestly, that's all I can really afford anyway on an aide's salary, to be completely honest with you. Every penny I make goes straight to rent and groceries, not that I have much of an appetite lately with all this stress. But no, to answer your question, absolutely nothing like that. I need all my wits about me just to survive the day.

...thoughts are being controlled? Or that someone is putting thoughts into your head?

Well, doctor, I... I wouldn't say they're putting thoughts *in* my head, exactly, but... but there's this whole other thing, and it's just as bad, maybe worse. It's about my things. My private things. You see, I paint a little bit. Watercolors, mostly. Just flowers and landscapes, things to try and calm my nerves when I get home. And I have my client papers, too—schedules, care plans, things I need for work. 

But a few months ago, I just... I knew, I absolutely *knew* that this other home-care agency in town—the one over on Elm Street, you know?—and some people from the public library downtown, they were watching my paintings and my papers. I got it in my head, and I know it's true. They were watching them to steal a chance that was meant for me. A promotion, maybe, or some kind of recognition for my art, or... or just my livelihood! I'd come home and I'd look at my watercolors drying on the kitchen table, and I could just feel their eyes on them. I'd move my work folders from the counter to the drawer, then from the drawer to under my mattress, just trying to hide them from these people. 

And I tried to tell people about it. I told my sister, I told one of my nicer clients, Mrs. Higgins. And they all looked at me like I was crazy. They told me it made no sense, that the library doesn't care about my watercolors and the other agency doesn't know who I am. But they don't understand, doctor. They don't see how everything is connected. Even when they were telling me it was impossible, I still *knew* they were doing it. I could feel it in my bones. It's like... like they're trying to take my future right out from under me, just by looking at my things. And it's so exhausting, trying to protect my papers and my little paintings every single day, on top of the voices and the feeling of being watched all the time. It's just... it's too much for one person to handle, it really is.
